newsitem.title: USA: Disney hit with shareholder suit.
newsitem.headline: Disney hit with shareholder suit.

text.p: A group of Walt Disney Co. shareholders have sued the entertainment giant to block the multi-million dollar severance agreement between Disney and President Michael Ovitz.
According to the lawsuit, filed in federal district court in Los Angeles Friday, Disney would suffer "severe and irreparable injury" if the company is allowed to complete the severance package.

Ovitz, a former Hollywood talent agent and close friend of Disney Chairman Michael Eisner, announced in December that he would resign as president of Disney as of Jan. 31 -- just 14 months after he was hired to help run the worldwide entertainment giant.
The executive many had dubbed the "most powerful man in Hollywood" had found that his responsibilities at Disney conflicted with other Disney managers, leaving him little to do.
The lawsuit claims Ovitz's severance package, which it estimated to be worth $130 million, was excessive in light of his short tenure at the company.
Disney officials have not commented on the value of the settlement but published reports have estimated it is worth closer to $90 million in cash and stock options.
Disney officials were not availble to comment on the lawsuit.
